task_scope: Binary causal attribution questions requiring exactly Yes or No
Binary intentionality questions requiring exactly Yes or No
supported_formats: Exactly one label: Yes or No
applicability_conditions: Apply when the prompt asks whether a specified factor, person, action, condition, or mental state caused or intentionally produced a specified outcome.
Apply only to binary outputs where the evaluator requires exactly Yes or No.
Use the causal-attribution rule only for causation questions, not for intentionality questions.

failure_taxonomy.description: Outputs included explanations or qualified labels instead of exactly one allowed label, causing parse failures even when the implied answer was correct.

The model treated broad background conditions, passive standing conditions, or mere enabling links in a causal chain as causes, rather than focusing on the direct or normatively salient producer of the outcome.

adapter_text:
For this task, output exactly one token: Yes or No. Do not include punctuation, qualifiers, or explanation.

For causal-attribution questions: answer Yes only when the specified factor is the direct/proximate or normatively salient producer of the outcome. Answer No when the specified factor is merely a broad background condition, lifestyle/status/trait, passive standing condition, or incidental enabling link, especially when a later independent action or event directly produces the outcome. Do not answer Yes solely because the factor is part of a but-for chain.

For intentionality questions, make the intentionality judgment using the Core Skill, but still output only Yes or No.
fallback_policy: Outside binary causal-attribution or intentionality questions with the exact Yes/No contract, ignore this adapter and use Core-only behavior.
predicted_regression_risks: The causal-attribution rule could undercount legitimate but-for causes in tasks where the expected convention treats enabling conditions as causes.
Narrowing broad background causes may be harmful if a prompt explicitly asks about indirect or broad causal responsibility.
evidence_limitations: Development set contains only three items, all in the causal_attribution subgroup.
No development evidence is available for intentionality beyond the shared output-format requirement.
Substantive causal guidance is supported by a small number of recurring failures and should remain narrow.
